keyFindings.text: A doctor-side contract for exactly this scoring surface already exists: the explicit lane's `PHRASE_BOOST_BOUND = { min: -1.0, max: 2.0 }` is documented as the same range the doctor skill-advisor proposal validator enforces via `phrase_boost_range` in `.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-skill-advisor-tune.yaml` — so `/doctor:skill-advisor` is already the sanctioned tuning surface for advisor phrase boosts and negative disambiguation. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:107-112] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-skill-advisor-tune.yaml]

Command bridges have a drift guard: `runtime/tests/command-bridges-drift-guard.vitest.ts` compares the generated projection, the generator dump and the allow-list, which is the natural CI seam for admitting doctor bridges and asserting they stay byte-stable. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/command-bridges-drift-guard.vitest.ts:1-40]

Command recommendations are rank-adjusted: in fusion ordering, a recommendation with `kind === 'command'` is demoted by 0.08 when the prompt does not itself contain a `/` character, so natural-language prompts do not float command bridges above skills by accident. This is the existing guard the doctor design must respect. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:776-777] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/types.ts:47]

Commands are already first-class scoring projections with `kind: 'command'`: `projection.ts` defines hand-authored `CommandBridgeProjection` entries (`command-spec-kit`, `memory:save`, `command-memory-save`, `create:agent`, `create:manual-testing-playbook`) plus a generated block of command bridges, and both the SQLite and filesystem projection loaders append the routing-enabled bridges to the skill list. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/projection.ts:75-151] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/projection.ts:1127] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/projection.ts:1205]

No doctor command participates in that surface today: `projection.ts` contains zero `doctor` references and zero `command-doctor-*` ids, and the only `doctor` mention in the advisor runtime source is the comment describing the tune proposal validator. `.skilled/commands/doctor/` itself carries no `command-metadata.json`, so the derive script has no input for it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:108-109] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/projection.ts]

Routing vocabulary for skills lives in each skill's `graph-metadata.json` (`intent_signals` plus `derived.trigger_phrases`); a skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter `trigger_phrases` and `intent_signals` are not read by any runtime routing reader, and reference/asset doc frontmatter `trigger_phrases` feed routing only when `SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS=true`. This means a doctor-routing change cannot be expressed by editing `SKILL.md` frontmatter alone. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md:338] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:36]

Scoring is a five-lane fusion (`explicit_author`, `lexical`, `graph_causal`, `derived_generated`, `semantic_shadow`) with per-variant weight multipliers (e.g. `explicit_author: 1.04`, `lexical: 1.00`, `graph_causal: 0.98`, `derived_generated: 0.98` in the default variant) and bounded constants in `weights-config.ts`. Any doctor-routing design lands inside this fusion, not beside it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:169-177] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/weights-config.ts:15-21]

The advisor has exactly one front door: `.skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs` resolves `runtime/dist/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.js` inside the `system-skill-advisor` package and spawns it with the caller's arguments; a freshness preflight refuses a stale or missing dist with exit 69 (75 for `--warm-only` retryable warmups). [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs:22-23] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs:70-83] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs:105-109]

The explicit-author lane already carries command syntax: a `PHRASE_BOOSTS` table maps exact command strings and phrases to skill ids and pseudo-command ids (for example `/speckit:save` → `memory:save` 1.6 / `command-memory-save` 1 / `system-spec-kit` 0.45; `/deep:research` → `system-deep-loop` 1.6 / `command-spec-kit` 0.45), and a `TOKEN_BOOSTS` table maps single tokens to skills. There is no `/doctor:*` entry in either table. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:117-119]

The generated command inventory is produced by `runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs` from per-skill `command-metadata.json` files plus a hand-maintained `allow-list.json`; the generated summary reports 19 command-metadata entries, 8 allow-list entries, 27 generated bridges, with TypeScript-active count 5 and Python-active count 15 — most generated bridges are `routingEnabled: false`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:28-40] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/command-bridges.generated.json:1-10]

The package exposes nine stable command ids (`advisor_recommend`, `advisor_rebuild`, `advisor_status`, `advisor_validate`, `skill_graph_scan`, `skill_graph_query`, `skill_graph_status`, `skill_graph_validate`, `skill_graph_propagate_enhances`) over a resident daemon; exit taxonomy is 0/1/64/69/75, and when the daemon is unreachable the CLI answers from the local Python scorer and marks the result degraded instead of failing. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md:318-336]

The prompt-time hook fires on every user prompt: kill-switch check, prompt gate, one bounded CLI `advisor_recommend` call, then a model-visible `Advisor:` brief; when there is no route it emits a directives fallback status line (`Advisor: no skill matched.`, `Advisor: prompt skipped.`, `Advisor: outage (<status>)`) and never blocks the prompt. Raw prompt text is not persisted. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md:33-43]

`check my git hooks` routes to `sk-git` with `confidence 0.8316`, `score 0.579682`, `dominantLane: explicit_author`, `status: active` — consistent with the explicit lane's `git -> sk-git 1.0` token boost rather than any hooks or doctor vocabulary. The recommendation names the skill, not `/doctor:git` or `/doctor:git setup`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-03.json] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:37]

`help me get started with this repo` routes to `sk-doc` with `confidence 0.82`, `score 0.229089`, `dominantLane: lexical`, plus a `compiledRoute` with `action: "defer"` and no targets. A getting-started/onboarding prompt is answered with a documentation skill on a weak lexical match. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-11.json]

All 12 measured calls exit 0 against a live advisor: `freshness: "live"`, `trustState.generation: 1033`, `confidenceThreshold: 0.8`, `uncertaintyThreshold: 0.35`. The measurement is reproducible from `events/measure-iter2-index.json`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-index.json]

Each payload carries a `_shadow` block (`advisor-shadow-learned-weights-v1`, `liveWeightsFrozen: true`) with parallel shadow scores for every emitted recommendation — a read-only learned-weights telemetry path that could inform later calibration but does not affect live routing. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-03.json]

Every empty result is a genuine no-route outcome under a live graph — the envelopes show `freshness: "live"` and no degradation marker, so the gaps are vocabulary/ownership gaps rather than staleness or daemon failure. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-10.json]

No recommendation in the sample carries `kind: "command"`; both non-empty results are skills (`sk-git`, `sk-doc`). Combined with iteration 1, this confirms doctor commands cannot appear as candidates until something introduces them to the projection. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-03.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-11.json]

Ten of the twelve prompts return **zero recommendations** (`recommendations: []`), so the hook would render `Advisor: no skill matched.` for them: `help me set up skilled`, `is my repo set up right`, `why is this rule not enforced`, `set up my repo correctly`, `verify my repository health`, `is the skill setup working`, `my hooks are not running`, `check if my environment is configured properly`, `something is wrong with my setup`, and `are my rules being enforced`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-01.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-04.json]

The measurement preserves raw artifacts: twelve per-prompt envelopes plus an index with exit code, duration, byte size and prompt text are on disk in the lineage for later regression baselining. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-index.json]

The recommendation gate is confidence (0.8), not raw score: a `0.229089` score still surfaces at `0.82` confidence. Routing-accuracy work therefore has to consider calibration behaviour, not only phrase coverage. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-11.json]

Three of the four topic-named example prompts return an empty recommendation — `help me set up skilled`, `is my repo set up right`, `why is this rule not enforced` — and only `check my git hooks` routes. The flagship onboarding phrase in the research topic has no advisor owner today. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-01.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-02.json] [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-03.json]

`_routes.yaml` is not a complete doctor-family inventory: `/doctor:env` exists as a standalone thin router (`env.md` with its own workflow and presentation assets) but appears nowhere in the manifest; `/doctor:update` is tracked only under a `standalone` node and `/doctor:mcp` only under `mcp_subroutes`. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/env.md:1-40] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:291-355]

`_routes.yaml` is the canonical route manifest for the routed doctor commands: it declares `/doctor:speckit` (speckit-retrieval), `/doctor:deep-loop`, six `/doctor:skill-advisor` targets, `/doctor:runtime-mirrors`, `/doctor:sk-code` setup, and three `/doctor:git` targets (hooks, standards, setup). [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:41-289]

`router-reach` already validates routing accuracy as a doctor workflow: it probes the live advisor for every declared phrase through `ci-router-vocabulary-reach.cjs` and reports. Any proposed routing-accuracy test can reuse this seam instead of inventing one. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:179-194]

Doctor commands are thin routers with a mandatory input gate: the target must be named explicitly, and the router must not infer it "from conversation history, open files, earlier runs or repository state". A plain-word advisor brief therefore has to name both the command and its target (for example `/doctor:git setup`) rather than only the command. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/skill-advisor.md:13-19] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/git.md:13-18]

Each doctor command doc carries an owner marker in an HTML comment — `<!-- skill_agent: system-skill-advisor -->`, `<!-- skill_agent: sk-git -->`, `<!-- skill_agent: system-spec-kit -->` — a latent machine-readable owner link a bridge generator could consume. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/skill-advisor.md:5] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/git.md:5] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/env.md:5]

Each route carries machine-readable fields: `command`, `target`, `yaml`, `setup_vars`, `allowed_flags`, `mutating` class, `gate3_location`, `mcp_tools`, `script_invocations` and `trigger_phrases` — a ready-made structured inventory for any advisor bridge. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:23-33]

Setup-shaped routes are read-only batteries: `/doctor:sk-code setup` runs `sk-code-setup-check.cjs` (optional `--prompt=<text>`), and `/doctor:git setup` runs `git-setup-check.cjs` (optional `--tool=<name>`); mutation lives in `/doctor:git hooks` (git config keys) and `/doctor:git standards` (`.sk-git/`). [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:220-289]

The `/doctor:skill-advisor` family is already the advisor's own health surface: `tune` mutates the scorer lanes (`explicit.ts`, `lexical.ts`, per-skill `graph-metadata.json`), `rebuild` mutates `skill-graph.sqlite` behind a backup, and `skill-graph-freshness`, `router-reach`, `skill-budget`, `parent-skill` are read-only audits. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:81-194]

The declared trigger phrases are already written in plain user language, e.g. git setup's `check my git hooks setup` / `is my sk-git setup working` / `which git rules are live`, git hooks' `pre-commit gate keeps blocking` / `disable comment hygiene gate`, and sk-code setup's `verify my sk-code surface` / `does my sk-code surface route`. These closely paraphrase the measured prompt set, so the vocabulary gap is about harvesting, not authoring. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:248-289]

The manifest has CI teeth: `route-validate.sh` asserts it against on-disk YAML assets, each owning router's frontmatter allowed-tools union, and internal consistency rules, with a documented dependency on python3 + PyYAML and exit codes 0/1/2/3. Any harvest change must keep this validator green. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/route-validate.sh:1-30]

The manifest states its own advisor status: the `trigger_phrases` are **not harvested by either Skill Advisor implementation**. Both harvesters only walk `.skilled/skills/*/{references,assets}/*.md` frontmatter (Python `_DOC_HARVEST_SUBDIRS = ("references","assets")` and the TS doc-frontmatter reader, which in this runtime is additionally gated by `SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS=true`), so a YAML file under `.skilled/commands/doctor/` is out of scope by both file type and root; doctor dispatch is presentation-menu/argv driven, and the field is retained "for a possible future doctor-routes harvester but is inert today". [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:14-21]

`routingEnabled` is driven per platform by `scoring-compatibility.json` runtime enablement; the generator only emits keywords, intent signals, description and name for an enabled runtime, and renders inactive bridges with empty signal lists. TypeScript-active count is 5, Python-active 15. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:250-290] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/command-bridges.generated.json:1-10]

Allow-list entries require `id`, `command`, `skillId`, `ownerMode` and a `reason`, and exist for commands whose owning skill has no `command-metadata.json` yet (for example the `/speckit:*` family and the retired `/memory:save` id). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/allow-list.json:1-50]

Bridge ids are derived from the command string and must match `^\/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-z0-9-]+$`; duplicates are rejected by an explicit uniqueness assertion. Because `/doctor:git` owns three targets (hooks, standards, setup), a naive one-bridge-per-route design would collide on `command-doctor-git` — doctor admission needs either a single bridge per command with target phrases in its signal lists, or allow-list ids that do not follow the command-derived form. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:56-60] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:117-130]

Command admission has exactly two inputs: a per-skill `command-metadata.json` (`derive-command-bridges.cjs:71`) or a hand-maintained `allow-list.json` entry; only three skills carry metadata today (`system-deep-loop`, `sk-design`, `sk-doc`), yielding the 19 metadata entries counted in the generated summary. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:71-99] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/command-bridges.generated.json:1-10]

Consequence for doctor routing: neither harvest path can see `.skilled/commands/doctor/**` (wrong root and wrong file type in both implementations), while the command-bridge pipeline cannot see route-level granularity unless doctor entries are authored per command with target phrases folded into their signal lists. Both supported mechanisms therefore require authored metadata, not direct consumption of `_routes.yaml`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:65-99] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:991-1051]

Everything above is guarded: the drift guard compares committed projections against a fresh generator dump and the allow-list, and `route-validate.sh` guards the doctor manifest, so any admission change has two CI gates to satisfy. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/tests/command-bridges-drift-guard.vitest.ts:1-40] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/route-validate.sh:1-30]

Harvested doc triggers land in the `skill_docs` table with content-hash-based upsert/delete semantics, and the derived lane consumes them with a bounded contribution (top 3 docs, 0.45 cap) so doc volume cannot dominate curated skill signals. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts:855-945] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/derived.ts:22-35]

Metadata entries require `command` and `ownerMode` but the authored shape carries far more routing-relevant material: `description`, `argumentHint`, `userIntent.job`, `userIntent.ownedSignals`, `choreography[]` and `discriminator.whenToUse` / `preferSiblingWhen` — a ready model for a doctor command entry. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/command-metadata.json:1-50]

The Python harvester roots at `.skilled/skills` (`SKILLS_DIR = SCRIPT_DIR/../../..`) and reads doc frontmatter only from `("references", "assets")` subdirectories of each skill directory when building its signal map. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:44] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:991] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:1030-1051]

The TypeScript harvester mirrors that scope with `HARVEST_SUBDIRS = ['references', 'assets']`, walking markdown files under those subdirs of each skill root, and is gated by `SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:170] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:204-217]

A fed phrase would score by `phraseSpecificity`: one token = 0.7, each extra token +0.18, capped at 1.0. A three-token doctor phrase like `check my git hooks setup` therefore scores 1.0 on an exact mention, the same order as the hand-written command boosts. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/text.ts:71-74]

Bridge `keywords` and `intentSignals` are consumed inside the explicit-author lane: for every projection skill (including command bridges), each phrase that appears with a word boundary adds `phraseSpecificity` to that id and records `author:<phrase>` evidence. Admission is therefore not a new scoring path; it reuses the strongest existing lane. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:358-376]

Command-kind recommendations do not ride a slash bonus: fusion demotes a `kind: 'command'` candidate by 0.08 when the prompt contains no `/`, so a doctor bridge reached from natural language starts with a small handicap. The handicap is uniform across all command bridges and does not block a strong phrase match. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/fusion.ts:776-777]

Measured contrast to design against: `check my git hooks` routed to `sk-git` at 0.83 while the manifest already declares the near-identical `check my git hooks setup` phrase; the feed decision is therefore about arbitration (which id owns which phrase), not about inventing vocabulary. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/034-doctor-command-guidance/research/lineages/deepseek-flash-max/events/measure-iter2-03.json] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:285-289]

Mechanism A - extend the harvesters to parse `_routes.yaml`: rejected. Both harvesters are hard-scoped to skill roots and the `references`/`assets` subdirs (Python `SKILLS_DIR` + `_DOC_HARVEST_SUBDIRS`; TS `HARVEST_SUBDIRS`), so this needs a new root, a new file type, YAML parsing in two languages, and new gate semantics, for a manifest that already documents the boundary as out of scope. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:44] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:170]

Mechanism B - hand-write `PHRASE_BOOSTS` entries for doctor phrases: rejected as the primary path. It is a supported code path, but it bypasses the command inventory, the generated projections, Python parity and the drift guard, and it silently changes scoring vocabulary outside the doctor tune flow; keep it for negative disambiguation only, where the tune contract (`phrase_boost_range`) already sanctions it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:107-200]

Mechanism C - admit doctor routes as command bridges through `allow-list.json` + `scoring-compatibility.json`: supported today. Allow-list ids are free-form (only non-empty string checks) while uniqueness is enforced per id, so `/doctor:git`'s three targets can take distinct ids such as `command-doctor-git-hooks` and `command-doctor-git-setup` without colliding; target phrases enter `keywords`/`intentSignals` and regeneration writes both TypeScript and Python projections. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:100-130] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:240-290]

Mechanism D - generate those admission inputs from `_routes.yaml` at build time so the manifest stays canonical: this is the recommended long-term shape. The manifest already carries `trigger_phrases` per route and the command docs carry `skill_agent` owner markers; route-validate.sh can assert the generated bridge set, and the drift guard keeps the projections byte-stable. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/_routes.yaml:36-38] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/command-bridges/derive-command-bridges.cjs:399-420]

Rendering carries the kind through and renders a label: the brief line is `Advisor: <freshness>; use <label> <confidence>/<uncertainty> pass.` with the label resolved from metadata or the recommendation name, and prepared commands keep `kind: 'command'`. A doctor bridge's rendered `name` is therefore what the user actually sees, so it should be the runnable command form (e.g. `/doctor:git setup`), not an internal bridge id. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:170] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/render.ts:439-447]

The input gate constrains the rendered guidance: because doctor routers refuse to infer a target, the bridge entry for a routed target must render a fully qualified name (`/doctor:git setup`) and the phrase set must be target-specific; one bridge per *route*, not per command, is the correct granularity. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/git.md:13-18]
